title: Missing indentation
explanation: Python uses indentation to know which lines belong to an if, for, while, def or class. After a line ending in a colon, the next line must be indented.
where: The line right after the one ending in ':'.

title: Unexpected indentation
explanation: This line is indented more than Python expected. Lines in the same block must line up exactly.
where: The reported line — compare its left edge with the line above.

pattern: IndentationError: unindent does not match any outer indentation level
title: Indentation doesn't line up
explanation: When you end a block, the next line must line up with some earlier block. Mixing tabs and spaces often causes this.
where: The reported line; check for tabs vs spaces.

title: Tabs and spaces mixed
explanation: The file mixes tab characters and spaces for indentation. Pick one (4 spaces is standard).
where: The reported line's leading whitespace.

title: Missing colon
explanation: if, elif, else, for, while, def and class lines must end with a colon ':'.
where: The end of the reported line.

pattern: SyntaxError: (unexpected EOF|'\(' was never closed|'\[' was never closed|'\{' was never closed)
title: Unclosed bracket
explanation: A bracket, parenthesis or brace was opened but never closed, so Python reached the end of the file still waiting.
where: Count the ( [ { on the reported line and the lines before it.

title: Extra closing bracket
explanation: There is a closing bracket with no matching opening bracket.
where: The reported line.

pattern: SyntaxError: (unterminated string literal|EOL while scanning string literal)
title: String never closed
explanation: A string started with a quote but the matching closing quote is missing on that line.
where: The reported line — look for a missing " or '.

pattern: SyntaxError: invalid syntax\. Maybe you meant '==' or ':=' instead of '='\?
title: = used where == was needed
explanation: A single = assigns a value. To compare two values (for example in an if), use ==.
where: The condition on the reported line.

title: Python can't read this line
explanation: Something on this line isn't valid Python: a missing operator, a stray character, or a keyword used incorrectly. Python often points at the character just after the real mistake.
where: The reported line and the end of the line before it.

title: Unknown name
explanation: You used a variable or function name that Python doesn't know at this point. It may be misspelled, defined later, defined inside another function, or missing quotes if you meant text.
where: Spelling and capitalization of the name; where it's first assigned.

title: Variable used before it's assigned in this function
explanation: Inside a function, assigning to a name makes it local for the whole function. Reading it before that assignment fails.
where: The first use of the variable inside the function.

pattern: TypeError: can only concatenate str \(not "([^"]+)"\) to str
title: Adding text and a number
explanation: + between a string and a number isn't allowed. Convert the number with str(), or use an f-string.
where: The + on the reported line.

title: Operator used on incompatible types
explanation: This operator doesn't work between these two types — often a string read from input() that was never converted to int or float.
where: The operands on the reported line; check where each value came from.

title: Calling something that isn't a function
explanation: You put ( ) after a value that isn't a function — or you reused a function's name (like list or str) as a variable.
where: The name followed by ( on the reported line.

title: Wrong number of arguments
explanation: The function was called with a different number of arguments than it was defined with.
where: Compare the call with the def line of that function.

title: Using [ ] on something that isn't a list/string/dict
explanation: Square brackets only work on sequences and dictionaries. This value is a different type (often None or an int).
where: The value before [ on the reported line.

title: Index isn't an integer
explanation: List and string positions must be whole numbers. A value read with input() is a string — convert it with int().
where: The expression inside [ ] on the reported line.

pattern: ValueError: invalid literal for int\(\) with base 10
title: Text that isn't a whole number
explanation: int() was given text that isn't a whole number (maybe empty, a decimal, or containing spaces).
where: The value passed to int(); print it to check.

pattern: ValueError: could not convert string to float
title: Text that isn't a number
explanation: float() was given text that isn't a number.
where: The value passed to float().

pattern: ValueError: (not enough|too many) values to unpack
title: Unpacking the wrong number of values
explanation: You assigned to several variables at once (a, b = ...) but the right side has a different number of items — common with input().split().
where: The left and right sides of the assignment.

title: Index past the end
explanation: You asked for a position that doesn't exist. Valid indices run from 0 to len - 1.
where: The index on the reported line; check loop bounds (range(len(x)) not range(len(x) + 1)).

title: Missing dictionary key
explanation: You read a key that isn't in the dictionary. Check spelling, or use .get() or 'key in d' first.
where: The key used on the reported line.

title: No such method or attribute
explanation: This type of value doesn't have the method or attribute you used — a typo, or the value isn't the type you expected (often None).
where: The name after the dot on the reported line.

title: Using a value that is None
explanation: The value is None — usually a function that doesn't return anything, or a method like list.sort() that changes the list and returns None.
where: Where this value was assigned.

title: Division by zero
explanation: You divided (/, // or %) by zero. Check the divisor before dividing.
where: The divisor on the reported line.

title: Recursion never stops
explanation: The function keeps calling itself without reaching a base case, or the recursive call doesn't move closer to it.
where: The base case condition and the argument of the recursive call.

pattern: EOFError: EOF when reading a line
title: Reading more input than was given
explanation: input() was called more times than there are lines of input.
where: How many times input() runs, especially inside loops.

title: Module not available
explanation: That module isn't installed in this sandbox. These exercises only need the standard library.
where: The import line.

title: Time limit exceeded
explanation: The program ran too long — usually an infinite loop whose condition never becomes false, or a program waiting for input that never comes.
where: Loop conditions: does something inside the loop change them?
